subject.title: feat: let plugins control inbound debounce policy

question: Should inbound debounce remain a plugin-owned WhatsApp policy hook, become operator-owned per-conversation WhatsApp configuration, or be generalized across all channel implementations before a public hook is shipped?
rationale: The alternatives establish different permanent plugin API, configuration, ownership, and precedence contracts; repository policy does not permit automation to choose that product boundary.

options.title: Sponsor hook-only policy
options.body: Keep the plugin hook, remove the new direct/group `debounceMs` fields, explicitly document WhatsApp-only support for now, and require live installed-plugin proof.

options.title: Sponsor config-only policy
options.body: Continue with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100970 and close this broader hook branch after preserving any uniquely needed rich-message fixes.

options.title: Require channel-generic hook
options.body: Delay publication until sibling channel owners can invoke the same contract consistently and prove shared semantics.

recommendation.title: Sponsor hook-only policy
recommendation.body: Keep the plugin hook, remove the new direct/group `debounceMs` fields, explicitly document WhatsApp-only support for now, and require live installed-plugin proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent ownership signal for WhatsApp inbound and delivery behavior and were directly asked to decide this contract.
